recentItems.title: Tightrope walker connects Europe's tallest slag heaps | DW News
recentItems.description:
French tightrope walker Tatiano-Mosio Bongonga spanned the 400 meters between Europe's two tallest slag heaps – performing acrobatic feats at 80 meters above ground along the way. The slag heaps of Los-en-Gohelle are the byproduct of almost a century of coal mining activity – and one of a handful of former mining sites with UNESCO World Heritage status.

recentItems.title: Why Germany's political center is losing ground | DW News
recentItems.description:
A "disaster" for Chancellor Friedrich Merz. Another win for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), this time in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. In Berlin, the Left party comes out on top — and fresh signs of Germany's political center becoming weaker. We take a closer look with Olaf Böhnke Managing Director in Germany of Rasmussen Global, the geopolitical advisory firm of former NATO Secretary General Anders Fogh Rasmussen.

recentItems.title: Ukraine launched 'biggest' drone attack on final day of Russian elections | DW News
recentItems.description:
The last day of Russia's elections were overshadowed by Ukrainian drone strikes on Moscow. More than 110 million Russians were eligible to vote, in elections widely criticised due to the lack of political opposition to President Vladimir Putin's policies. Russian media reports that the Kremlin-backed United Russia Party has easily won the parliamentary election. DW correspondent Sergei Satanovskii and Chatham House Russia analyst Nikolai Petrov discuss the results.

recentItems.title: German chancellor calls state election a 'disaster' for his party but vows to stay on | DW News
recentItems.description:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's conservative CDU is dealt a massive blow in two state elections. In the eastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania the far-right Alternative for Germany won its second regional election victory in succession. And the CDU may even fall short of the five percent threshold needed to enter parliament. In the capital Berlin, Merz's party has lost its role at the head of the state government.
